processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length were grown by the Bridgman method (10–15 mm/h pulling rate); the crystal growth with subsequent cooling occurred within a time period of about 12 h.

The 250 °C/14 day anneal gives the maximum degree of short-range ordering (highest x-ray scattering intensity); its hardness equals that of the as-grown monocrystal. Short heat treatments at temperatures up to 300 °C were performed in an argon atmosphere of 99.99% purity.

structures.overall_structure: (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal (single crystal) in the state of maximum short-range order (K-state) after the 250 °C/14 day anneal.

phases_present.phase_name: Fe-16%Al solid solution with short-range order (K-state)

inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm

grain_structure.texture: (111) oriented monocrystal (single crystal, no grain boundaries)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Fischerscope H100 microhardness tester (maximum load 1 N); HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]; reported HU values are averages of more than 40 measurements

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: none (equal hardness to the as-grown monocrystal; heat-treatment effect on HU only about 5–10% at most)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; HU = F/(26.43·h²); averages of more than 40 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: to determine the effect of heat treatment / state of atomic order on the hardness of (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 250 °C/14 day anneal (maximum short-range order) gives the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal; heat treatment shifts HU by only about 5–10% around 2000 N/mm².

characterization_methods.technique: X-ray scattering (characterisation of degree of short-range order)
characterization_methods.purpose: to characterise the degree of short-range atomic ordering
characterization_methods.key_findings: The highest degree of short-range ordering (highest x-ray scattering intensity) was observed at 250 °C; the 250 °C/14 day anneal gives the maximum ordering state. (Ordering studied in a separate study, refs [16,20].)

unmapped_findings: The highest degree of short-range ordering (characterised by x-ray scattering intensity) was observed at 250 °C for isochronal annealings of Fe-18%Al for 14 days; the activation energy for this ordering reaction was found to be only 0.3 eV/atom and 100 h were sufficient at 250 °C for reaching a near-equilibrium state (SRO study reported in separate refs [16,20]).
Quenching from 1100 °C suppressed short-range ordering nearly completely, giving the minimum-ordering state.

Short-range ordering in the studied Fe-Al alloys, controlled by heat treatments below 600 °C, has no major impact on the deformation behaviour; only heat treatments above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys.
The 250 °C/14 day anneal produces the maximum degree of ordering but gives the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal, i.e. short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness.
No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320 °C (a different heat treatment than the 250 °C/14 d state of this sample).
